panels.rationale: Single clinical facial photograph of a newborn with captioned characteristic dysmorphic features of FASD. The image directly supports smooth philtrum and a thin upper vermilion; hypertrichosis and a flat nasal bridge are also captioned but are outside the supplied vocabulary. A measuring ruler is present, and the eyes are obscured for anonymization.

panels.figure_caption: Cardinal facial features of dysmorphology. Smooth philtrum, thin vermillion border of the upper lip, mild hypertrichosis, and a flat nasal bridge are evidenced here in John.
in_text_mentions: Our results added to a score of 15. It has been established that a score greater than 5 is consistent with FASD. Figure 1 and Figure 2 show the observed features of FASD in the newborn, namely, smooth philtrum, thin vermillion, railroad track ears, flat nasal bridge, and hypertrichosis.

panels.rationale: Single-panel clinical photograph of a newborn with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD), consistent with the article title and in-text description. The panel is a real patient image showing characteristic FASD manifestations: smooth philtrum and thin upper lip (supported by in-text and allowed vocabulary), plus additional FASD features (railroad track ears, flat nasal bridge, hypertrichosis) noted in the caption. A black annotation covers the eye, but this does not preclude inclusion. No other exclusions apply, and the image is of sufficient quality to identify clinical features.
